item.title: NASA's Swift space telescope plunges back to Earth in fiery demise
item.description:
NASA One of NASA’s leading space telescopes crashed down to Earth on Wednesday, less than three months after a last-ditch rescue mission failed. The Swift Observatory reentered Earth’s atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. ET over Indonesia’s North Sumatra region. Intense solar activity over the last few years dragged its orbit down. It is not yet clear how much of the 1.5-ton spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere. NASA said much of it did, though some components were expected to survive. Private company Katalyst Space had been hired to boost the telescope’s orbit. The company’s robotic craft launched in July but ran into trouble soon after, and it crashed back to Earth in September.
